units.title: Construct: Consuming typestate and explicit recovery after partial device writes
steps: Derive a lifecycle transition table including partially configured RecoveryRequired, token generation retirement and storage lifetime; distinguish C wrapper diagnostics from Rust moves.

Implement pt_device_init/configure/close/recover with consumed matching tokens, unchanged success-output on failure, and externally certified quiescence before cleanup. Fail after each of the two control writes.
checks: Failure after control3 consumes the old token, leaves ready output unchanged and returns RecoveryRequired. quiet0 retains control3; quiet1 clears it. Reusing the pre-failure token after recovery rejects.

Enumerate failure stage0/1/2, quiet0/1, copied stale tokens and UINT32_MAX retirement; compile the wrong-wrapper fixture and demonstrate that a copied correct wrapper still compiles. Reject false-CLOSED and ignored-generation mutants.
reasoning: Derive a lifecycle transition table including partially configured RecoveryRequired, token generation retirement and storage lifetime; distinguish C wrapper diagnostics from Rust moves.
deliverables: Implement pt_device_init/configure/close/recover with consumed matching tokens, unchanged success-output on failure, and externally certified quiescence before cleanup. Fail after each of the two control writes.

Enumerate failure stage0/1/2, quiet0/1, copied stale tokens and UINT32_MAX retirement; compile the wrong-wrapper fixture and demonstrate that a copied correct wrapper still compiles. Reject false-CLOSED and ignored-generation mutants.

Replace one synchronous control write with deferred DMA completion. Design an owning Recovery token that retains a buffer until quiescence, including reset while a stale alias survives; explain why generation checks cannot inspect a dangling pointer safely.

rubric.criterion: Derive a lifecycle transition table including partially configured RecoveryRequired, token generation retirement and storage lifetime; distinguish C wrapper diagnostics from Rust moves.

units.title: Construct: Staged builders, presence masks and cross-field admission
steps: Separate required-field presence from value validity and cross-field constraints; identify what staged C wrapper types can diagnose and what a public struct can bypass.

Implement one-shot setters and atomic finish for address, length and timeout using the exact bounds in CONTRACTS.md, and construct a second staged-wrapper interface with the same admitted configurations.
checks: address252,length8,timeout10 is fully present but rejects the extent. address4,length8,timeout10 succeeds. Repeating address does not silently overwrite it.

Enumerate all eight presence masks, every setter permutation, duplicate setters, alignment violations and the address+length boundary. Preserve output canaries on incomplete/invalid finish; reject omitted-mask and omitted-cross-field-check mutants.
reasoning: Separate required-field presence from value validity and cross-field constraints; identify what staged C wrapper types can diagnose and what a public struct can bypass.
deliverables: Implement one-shot setters and atomic finish for address, length and timeout using the exact bounds in CONTRACTS.md, and construct a second staged-wrapper interface with the same admitted configurations.

Add a mutually exclusive DMA or polling mode where DMA requires alignment and polling forbids a callback. Derive the new state space and compare type proliferation with a checked sum representation; the delayed variant permits safe replacement of one previously set field.

units.title: Construct: Dual binary session automata with bounded dialogue
steps: Derive dual send/receive traces for HELLO, ACCEPT, a bounded DATA/ACK loop and BYE; distinguish runtime protocol conformance from transport liveness and language-enforced session types.

Implement pt_session_step for both roles, phase and remaining count, rejecting wrong direction/tag and terminal reuse without progress. Build an in-process two-endpoint trace driver using only synthetic messages.
checks: At remaining0, HELLO and ACCEPT lead directly to BYE. A client receiving HELLO is rejected; an ACK reduces remaining exactly once.

Enumerate both roles, remaining0..8 and every phase/tag/direction, compare against a separately written transition table and assert rejected-state preservation. Reject direction-erasure and ACK-does-not-decrement mutants.
reasoning: Derive dual send/receive traces for HELLO, ACCEPT, a bounded DATA/ACK loop and BYE; distinguish runtime protocol conformance from transport liveness and language-enforced session types.

units.title: Construct: Hierarchical run-to-completion transitions and observable entry order
steps: Derive least-common-ancestor exit/entry paths, inherited FAIL handling, external self transitions and internal PING; distinguish this bounded HSM subset from full UML semantics.
Implement pt_dispatch with inner-first exits, outer-first entries, a nonreentry guard, and transactional trace-capacity failure. Produce a table-driven independent transition oracle.
checks: OFFLINE CONNECT emits exit OFFLINE, entry ONLINE, entry IDLE. BUSY START emits exit BUSY then entry BUSY. BUSY FAIL exits BUSY and ONLINE before entering FAULT.

Check every active leaf/event pair, insufficient trace capacity, repeated BUSY START and PING exhaustion. Reject reversed-entry and omitted-exit mutants; compare exact action sequences rather than final states alone.
reasoning: Derive least-common-ancestor exit/entry paths, inherited FAIL handling, external self transitions and internal PING; distinguish this bounded HSM subset from full UML semantics.
deliverables: Implement pt_dispatch with inner-first exits, outer-first entries, a nonreentry guard, and transactional trace-capacity failure. Produce a table-driven independent transition oracle.

Check every active leaf/event pair, insufficient trace capacity, repeated BUSY START and PING exhaustion. Reject reversed-entry and omitted-exit mutants; compare exact action sequences rather than final states alone.

Add an entry action that posts another event and a guard on the parent transition. Queue the posted event until the current run-to-completion step ends and define guard fallback; the delayed variant introduces a local transition that intentionally preserves a composite state.

units.title: Construct: Bounded active-object queue and failure-preserving dispatch
steps: Explain serialized event ownership, run-to-completion scheduling and the difference between event admission and successful handling in an MCU active object.

Compose the HSM with a four-slot copied-event ring; reject overflow unchanged and retain an event whose dispatch fails. Integrate learner-owned execution.tasks and sync.copied_queue through an explicit adapter.
checks: The fifth post to a full ring rejects. If CONNECT cannot fit its trace, head/count remain0/4 and OFFLINE stays active. Four successful steps reach FAULT.

steps: Explain switch-based continuation labels, automatic-local lifetimes, duplicate-label constraints and why suspension across an ordinary function return does not retain a C stack.

units.title: Construct: Memory behavior trees, running-child ownership and abort
steps: Derive the different control rules of sequence and selector nodes, and distinguish a memory tree from a reactive tree that rechecks earlier guards.

checks: A sequence with successful leaf1 and running leaf2 calls leaf1 once across two ticks, leaf2 twice, and aborts leaf2 exactly once on cancel.
